#First, I am going to plot a bar chart of mean cost dependent on brand. The response variable (dependent variable) is the mean cost (numeric, continuous). The focal predictor (independent variable) is the brand (categorical).

#Bar charts are plotted as a "barplot," and I need to create a barplot between a numerical and categorical column.

#Making the basic barplot:
> ggplot(brandmeancost, aes(x = brandmeancost$Brand, y = brandmeancost$`Mean Cost (Numerical)`))+geom_col(fill = "skyblue")   #Not good
> barplot(height = brandmeancost$`Mean Cost (Numerical)`, names = brandmeancost$Brand, col = 'skyblue')   #very good

#Improving the barplot:
> barplot(height = brandmeancost$`Mean Cost (Numerical)`, names = brandmeancost$Brand, col = 'skyblue', main = 'Mean Cost of Sampled Brands')   #Adds a title
> barplot(height = brandmeancost$`Mean Cost (Numerical)`, names = brandmeancost$Brand, col = 'skyblue', main = 'Mean Cost of Sampled Brands', las = 2)   #las argument changes the
                                                               orientation of the axis
                                                               labels: 0 = parallel to the
                                                               axis (default), 1 = 
                                                               horizontal to axis, 2 =
                                                               perpendicular to axis 
                                                               (what I did), 3 = vertical 
                                                               to the axis

#The best R graph tutorial website I found: https://r-graph-gallery.com/ I used this website to help improve my barplot, and it is great for a variety of other graph styles.
